_note: Song-level PREMISES (plan step 3, 14 Oct 2026). Assistant-authored in the main thread from brief/persona.md and material/ingredients.md; flagged (persona), NOT approved by Joe. Joe did not want to choose up front, so all three are built to a full hook (writing/premise_hooks.md) and he picks by ear. Each section has an ARGUMENT (a claim about the narrator), the MOVES its bars make, and the INGREDIENTS (ids in material/ingredients.md) it may draw on in any order. `python -m ww.write.premise --plan ID` turns one into a plan file argue_stage reads.

premises.title: Mr Worldwide on a shoestring
premises.one_line: He is a global high-roller whose fortune is a million in the wrong currency: every luxury he claims is priced, and the price is tiny.
trait_families: rich in the wrong currency (price over value)
buys tat and crowns himself with it

Hook 1-4.argument: I'm a millionaire abroad and skint at home: the money only works where it's worthless.

Hook 5-8.argument: My luxuries are real; they just cost less than a meal deal.

Hook 9-16.argument: My crown is a pink top hat and my estate is a garden gnome, and I'd do it all again for the price.

V1 9-16.argument: I don't get stranded, I get a free night under the stars with a mechanic thrown in.

V2 1-8.argument: I travel light: I leave the bike, the key and the helmet wherever they stop being useful.

premises.title: Been everywhere, seen nothing
premises.one_line: He has been to every main event on earth and can tell you nothing about any of them, because he was asleep, at the bar, or buying a gnome.
trait_families: sleeps through / misses the main event
buys tat and crowns himself with it

Hook 1-4.argument: I've been to every big show going and I can't tell you how one of them ended.

Hook 5-8.argument: The headliner was on, so I bought the gnome instead.

Hook 9-16.argument: Ask me about the waterfalls and I'll tell you about my boot; ask me about the film and I'll tell you about the carpet.

V1 9-16.argument: Being left behind is my best view of anywhere.

V2 1-8.argument: I did the whole of Vietnam; I just didn't do it on the bike I started on.

premises.title: The world as an errand
premises.one_line: He does the world the way other people do the big shop: a list, a queue, a receipt, and nothing on earth worth raising his voice for.
trait_families: files the epic as an errand
obeys the rules to the letter and wins

Hook 1-4.argument: Three countries on a bike is just my round; the hard bit is the ferry check-in.

Hook 5-8.argument: A bribe is a parking fine if you keep the receipt.

Hook 9-16.argument: Every border is a counter and I always have my number ready.

V1 9-16.argument: A breakdown in the desert is a booking with a late check-in.

V2 1-8.argument: I returned the bike to Vietnam, just not to the shop.
